payload.claim: The agent note "Give the critic cell's export a character outside ASCII, such as é in an added line of _ANCHORING_DIFF" is ambiguous about whether to mutate the shared module-level _ANCHORING_DIFF constant in tests/test_session.py (reused in roughly 78 other call sites, several asserting exact equality against it, e.g. assert critic[0][2] == _ANCHORING_DIFF, assert applies == [_ANCHORING_DIFF, grown], and others depending on specific lines sitting outside every hunk of it) or to build a locally-scoped derived diff for just this new test, following the file's own existing precedent _GROWN_PATCH = _ANCHORING_DIFF + "# the rebuttal's own fix\n". Read the mutating way, the change risks altering hunk shape that dozens of unrelated, currently-passing tests depend on; read the appending way (consistent with the _GROWN_PATCH precedent and with keeping the hunk anchored at src/x.py line 1), it is safe. The spec does not say which, so a builder could plausibly pick the risky reading, though the file's own convention and the line-1 anchoring instruction resolve the ambiguity for a careful reader.
